title: Data senior systemdesign multi team data platform
topic: Data senior systemdesign multi team data platform
question: How would you design a data platform that serves dozens of independent teams, each with their own pipelines and data needs, without it collapsing into chaos?
idealAnswer:
Design around self-service, provide shared infrastructure, e.g. ingestion frameworks, orchestration, storage, access control, as a platform teams can use independently, rather than a central team that builds every pipeline on request and becomes a bottleneck

Establish clear ownership and data contracts between teams, e.g. a team producing a dataset commits to a schema and quality bar, so consumers aren't broken by upstream changes made without warning, similar in spirit to API contracts between services

Provide strong governance and access control as platform features, e.g. centralized cataloging, lineage, and permissions, so teams get autonomy over their own data without the platform losing visibility or compliance

Standardize just enough to get interoperability, e.g. common table formats, naming conventions, orchestration tooling, while leaving room for teams to choose their own transformation logic and schemas within their domain, a data-mesh-style federated approach rather than one central team owning everything

Address the cultural and organizational side explicitly, e.g. incentivizing teams to adopt shared tooling through better developer experience and support, rather than mandating it, since a purely top-down mandate tends to get worked around

A strong answer discusses cost and multi-tenancy concerns, e.g. resource isolation and cost attribution so one team's expensive workload doesn't degrade performance or budget for others sharing the same infrastructure
